questions.explanation: Context prevents misunderstanding. A bare question may confuse the listener.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Introducing yourself and the register it calls for

stimulus.body: A new member addresses the whole club at a meeting.

questions.stem: A sports club member introduces themselves to the group. Which register fits?

options.text: Hi everyone, I am the new defender.
Good evening all, I am the new defender, honoured to join.
Yo club, defender here.
options.misconception: too casual for a group address

options.text: I am the new defender, that is all.

questions.explanation: A group address stays friendly and clear. Option A does that without being overly formal or curt.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Greetings and the hours they belong to
questions.stem: A sports club member arrives at noon. Which greeting fits?

options.text: Good morning.
Good afternoon.
Good evening.
Good night.

questions.explanation: Noon and after call for good afternoon. The others mismatch the time or are farewells.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Describing where a place is
questions.stem: A sports club member locates the locker room. Which reply is clearest?

options.text: It is opposite the pool, across the corridor.
Somewhere near the pool area.
Around the corner maybe.
You will find it if you look.

questions.explanation: A clear location states a relative position. Option A does that; the others are vague.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Describing the weather and its forecast
questions.stem: A sports club enjoys a sunny training day. How should the weather be described?

answer.exemplar: The weather should be described as sunny and warm, noting good conditions for outdoor training.

questions.explanation: Describing sun and warmth sets expectations. Omitting conditions leaves the note incomplete.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Saying how often a hobby happens

stimulus.body: A teammate asks how often you stretch. You stretch every day.

questions.stem: A sports club member answers about stretching. Which reply is accurate?

options.text: I stretch every day.
I stretch once a week.
I never stretch.
I stretch occasionally.

questions.explanation: Every day matches the stated habit. The others misstate frequency.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Telling a past experience
questions.stem: A sports club member finishes a story about a past match. Which closing is appropriate?

options.text: And that is how we won the cup.
Anyway, whatever, I am done.
I do not remember the rest.
The end, no more to say.

questions.explanation: A narrative closing wraps up the story. Option A does that; the others are abrupt or flat.
